lessons.title: Number Bases and Modular Arithmetic - JAMB Self-Tutoring Lesson
lessons.html:
Number Bases and Modular Arithmetic

This self-tutoring lesson covers Place value, conversion, operations in bases 2 to 10 and modular arithmetic. It follows the JAMB Mathematics topic structure and is designed so a student can study before attempting the 200-question practice bank.

Learning objectives

  • Explain the main ideas without memorising blindly.
  • Choose the correct rule or formula.
  • Solve worked examples step by step.
  • Check an answer for reasonableness.

How to study

  1. Read the explanation slowly.
  2. Copy the worked method onto paper.
  3. Cover the answer and reproduce the method yourself.
  4. Attempt the practice questions.
  5. Read the explanation even when correct.

Worked example method

Write the information given, identify the mathematical relationship, select the appropriate formula or rule, substitute carefully, simplify one line at a time, then check the result against the original question.

Common mistakes

  • Choosing a formula before understanding the question.
  • Skipping algebraic steps.
  • Rounding too early.
  • Ignoring signs, units, restrictions or the requested form.

Self-test checkpoint

Before continuing, explain the topic in your own words and solve one example without looking at the worked method. If you cannot, return to the explanation and try again.

Worked self-tutoring example

Question: Convert 5 in base ten to base 5.

  1. A. 5
  2. B. 6
  3. C. 4
  4. D. 10

Correct answer: 10

Step-by-step explanation: Divide repeatedly by 5 and read the remainders upward. The result is 10 in base 5. Now cover the answer and solve the question again without looking. Then explain aloud why the other three options are wrong.

Exam strategy

Read the complete question, identify what is known and what is required, estimate the expected size or form of the answer, calculate carefully and substitute the result back into the problem when possible.

Revision summary

The goal is understanding: you should know when a method applies, why it applies, and how to check your result.
